content.title: About
content.content: A vegetable sushi roll is a nori-wrapped roll that replaces fish with a fresh mix of vegetables such as cucumber, avocado, carrot, bell pepper and lettuce. It is usually served with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger, and is popular among vegetarians and those seeking a light, low‑calorie alternative to traditional sushi.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetable rolls appeared in Japan in the 1970s as a response to growing demand for vegetarian cuisine.
Nori sheets are rich in iodine and B‑group vitamins.
The combination of fresh vegetables makes the roll a source of vitamins A, C and K.
In Japan vegetable rolls are often called “katsu‑mori,” which translates to “vegetable roll.”
Traditional soy sauce served with rolls is fermented for at least six months.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The vegetables provide vitamin C for immune support and vitamin A important for vision.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: One roll typically contains 150–200 kcal, making it a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Nori contains omega‑3 fatty acids and antioxidants that benefit heart function.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: When soy sauce is used sparingly, the roll remains relatively low in salt.

items.title: Seaweed allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to nori.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Soy sauce can significantly increase sodium intake, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: If vegetables are not thoroughly washed, bacteria may be present in the roll.

items.title: Gluten in soy sauce
items.content: Traditional soy sauce contains wheat; gluten‑free versions should be used for celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The roll is conveniently eaten with chopsticks, cutting off bite‑size pieces. Dip each piece in soy sauce, add a dab of wasabi for heat, and eat pickled ginger between bites to cleanse the palate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared roll in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage keep the ingredients separate and assemble the roll just before serving.
